name: debrief
description: Maritime exercise analysis: catalogues of plots, a map, and Python analysis tools

viewsWelcome.contents:
Debrief keeps plots in catalogues: folders you choose.
[Add catalogue folder](command:debrief.addCatalogue)
[Create catalogue](command:debrief.createCatalogue)
New to Debrief? Five short walkthroughs work on a copy of the sample exercise.
[Start a walkthrough](command:debrief.walkthroughs)
Open a plot from a catalogue to see its tracks, annotations and sensor data here.
Every change to the open plot appears here. Undo returns the plot to an earlier step; nothing is lost.

walkthroughs.title: Open and explore a serial
walkthroughs.description: Serial 1 of the sample exercise: move through time, select tracks, compare them in the Tote and read the narrative in the Timeline. About 8 minutes.

steps.title: Open a copy of serial 1
steps.description:
Serial 1 of the sample exercise, 15 Jun 2023 from 08:00Z to 12:00Z: BLUE ONE gains RED ONE, a submarine, among merchant traffic east of Chesapeake Bay. You work on a copy, titled Serial 1: Open and explore a serial, so the sample itself never changes.

The copy goes into a catalogue of its own, Walkthrough: Open and explore a serial, in Catalogues.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the button and press Enter.

[Open a copy of serial 1](command:debrief.walkthrough.open?%5B%22explore%22%5D)

media.altText: The map of serial 1: BLUE ONE in blue and RED ONE in red among grey merchant tracks.

steps.title: Move current time
steps.description:
Drag the slider under the large current time in the time controller. Each track's position at that time is marked on the map with a square in its colour. **▶** plays; at 60× a minute of the exercise passes each second. The strip beneath is the whole plot: drag the shaded band, or its edges, to narrow what is drawn in full.

The time controller is **Time**, at the top of the Debrief sidebar.

**Keyboard:** Tab to **Current time**, the slider; ← and → step it, Page Up and Page Down step further, Home and End go to the window's ends. Space plays and pauses.

[Show the time controller](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22explore%22%2C%22debrief.time.focus%22%5D)

media.altText: The time controller under the map, with each track's position at current time marked by a square.

steps.title: Select tracks in the Outline
steps.description:
Click **BLUE ONE** in the Outline, then Ctrl-click **RED ONE** to add it (Cmd-click on macOS); Shift-click selects every row from the last one clicked, a range. The map outlines what is selected, and the tools offered change with the selection: with two tracks, **Closest approach** is on offer. The buttons above the Outline hide or show what is selected, colour it, select all, select a row's children, or clear the selection.

**Outline** is in the Debrief sidebar.

**Keyboard:** ↑ and ↓ move through the Outline; Enter selects, Ctrl+Shift+Enter adds to the selection (Cmd+Shift+Enter on macOS).

[Show the Outline](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22explore%22%2C%22debrief.outline.focus%22%5D)

media.altText: BLUE ONE and RED ONE selected on the map, the other tracks dimmed.

steps.title: Compare tracks in the Tote
steps.description:
In the Tote, choose **BLUE ONE** as the primary and add **RED ONE**. Each row is a measure, worked out at current time: range, true bearing, relative bearing (R to port, G to starboard), angle on the bow, bearing rate, and each track's course, speed and depth. Move current time and they follow.

**Tote** is below the time controller; it starts folded.

**Keyboard:** **Primary** and **Add** are lists: Tab to one, ↓ to choose. Or, on a track in the Outline, Shift+F10 opens its menu: **Set as Tote primary**, **Add to Tote**.

[Show the Tote](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22explore%22%2C%22debrief.tote.focus%22%5D)

media.altText: The Tote: a row for each measure, a column for BLUE ONE and one for RED ONE, with a thin line on the map between them.

steps.title: Read the narrative in the Timeline
steps.description:
The Timeline lists BLUE ONE's, RED ONE's and exercise control's logs in one time order. Choose an entry: current time moves to it, and the entry is shown beside its track on the map. While playing, the list follows current time.

**Timeline** is in the Debrief sidebar.

**Keyboard:** ↑ and ↓ move through the list; Enter chooses an entry; / searches.

[Show the Timeline](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22explore%22%2C%22debrief.timeline.focus%22%5D)

[Next walkthrough: Import and collate](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22debrief.debrief%23collate%22%2Ctrue%5D)

media.altText: The Timeline's entries in time order, the one at current time marked, and its text beside RED ONE on the map.

walkthroughs.title: Import and collate
walkthroughs.description: Import BLUE ONE's navigation log, see where each source has data, take the new data and choose which source supplies a period. About 8 minutes.

steps.title: Open a copy of serial 1
steps.description:
A fresh copy of serial 1, titled Serial 1: Import and collate, with BLUE ONE's navigation log ready to import beside it: a fix every 10 s for part of the serial, as new data would arrive after an exercise. The sample itself never changes.

The copy goes into a catalogue of its own, Walkthrough: Import and collate.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the button and press Enter.

[Open a copy of serial 1](command:debrief.walkthrough.open?%5B%22collate%22%5D)

media.altText: The map of serial 1, BLUE ONE's track highlighted.

steps.title: Import the navigation log
steps.description:
Import blue-one-nav-log.rep, a REP file. Debrief asks, for each track, whether it is plotted over the ground (OTG), each fix where it was logged, or by dead reckoning (DR); choose **Over the ground (OTG)**. The file is kept unchanged as a source, and the import is a plot of its own in the catalogue. A legacy Debrief .dpf plot is imported the same way.

Your own files: **Import plot file (REP, .dpf, Word, PDF)…** on Catalogues' title bar.

**Keyboard:** In each question, ↓ chooses and Enter imports.

[Import the navigation log](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22collate%22%2C%22debrief.walkthrough.importLog%22%5D)

media.altText: A REP file of fixes becoming a new item in the catalogue.

steps.title: See where each source has data
steps.description:
In the catalogue, the log is marked **✦ New data**: imported after the plot, sharing a platform with it and with data in its period. **Coverage** shows each of the plot's tracks with a bar for every source of its data, the periods each covers filled in.

**Coverage** is below Catalogues; it starts folded.

**Keyboard:** Tab moves through Coverage's tracks, bars and lists.

[Show Coverage](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22collate%22%2C%22debrief.showCoverage%22%5D)

media.altText: Coverage: BLUE ONE with two bars, the plot's own data and the navigation log's, overlapping for part of the serial.

steps.title: Take the new data
steps.description:
**Take** brings the log's data into the plot as one step: BLUE ONE gains fixes where it had none, and WATCHER, a contact the plot had not seen, is added. Undo takes it back.

**Take** is in Coverage; or **Take data into the open plot…** on the log's menu in Catalogues.

**Keyboard:** Tab to **Take** and press Enter.

[Take the new data](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22collate%22%2C%22debrief.takeNewData%22%5D)

media.altText: BLUE ONE's track extended by the log's fixes, and WATCHER added.

steps.title: Choose a source for a period
steps.description:
Where the plot and the log both have data for BLUE ONE, choose which supplies that period: the log's fixes are every 10 s, the plot's every minute. Pick the log in the period's list and press **Set**, or click its bar. One step, naming the item and the period.

In **Coverage**, under BLUE ONE.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the period's list, ↑ and ↓ to pick (nothing changes yet), then Enter or **Set**.

[Show Coverage](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22collate%22%2C%22debrief.coverage.focus%22%5D)

[Next walkthrough: Tidy a track](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22debrief.debrief%23tidy%22%2Ctrue%5D)

media.altText: Coverage with the log chosen to supply the period where the two overlap.

walkthroughs.title: Tidy a track
walkthroughs.description: Remove GPS glitches, smooth a track, mark and label a fix, and shear a leg as in TMA. About 10 minutes.

steps.title: Open a copy of serial 1, with glitches
steps.description:
A fresh copy of serial 1, titled Serial 1: Tidy a track. Three of RED ONE's fixes have been moved miles off its track, as GPS glitches would put them; the step that did it is in History, so it is never mistaken for real data. The sample itself never changes.

The copy goes into a catalogue of its own, Walkthrough: Tidy a track.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the button and press Enter.

[Open a copy of serial 1](command:debrief.walkthrough.open?%5B%22tidy%22%5D)

media.altText: RED ONE's track with three spikes where its glitched fixes are.

steps.title: Remove the jumps
steps.description:
A jump is a fix RED ONE could not have reached in time: faster than three times its median speed, and at least 10 kn. Select RED ONE and find its jumps: they are ringed on the map and listed, each ticked. Untick any that are real, then remove the rest, as one step.

**Find and remove jumps…** is on RED ONE's menu in the Outline.

**Keyboard:** Enter takes the threshold offered; in the list of jumps, Space ticks and unticks and Enter removes those ticked.

[Find jumps in RED ONE](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tidy%22%2C%22debrief.removeJumps%22%2C%22track-red-one%22%5D)

media.altText: RED ONE with its three jumps ringed.

steps.title: Smooth the track
steps.description:
Smoothing moves each fix to the average of itself and the fixes either side, over an odd number of fixes; the first and last stay where they are, and no time changes. Debrief shows the track as it would be, dashed, and how far fixes would move, before you apply it as one step.

**Smooth track…** is on the track's menu in the Outline.

**Keyboard:** Type the number of fixes and press Enter; then **Apply**.

[Smooth RED ONE](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tidy%22%2C%22debrief.smoothTrack%22%2C%22track-red-one%22%5D)

media.altText: RED ONE and, dashed beside it, the track as smoothing would leave it.

steps.title: Mark and label a fix
steps.description:
Give one fix a colour, a label or a comment of its own: the moment RED ONE turned, say. The fix list shows every fix with its time, position, course and speed; choose one, then its colour or **Label…**. Each change is one step, and the mark stays with its fix whatever else changes.

**Fixes: colour, label or comment…** is on the track's menu in the Outline; or right-click a fix on the map.

**Keyboard:** ↑ and ↓ move through the fix list; Enter chooses a fix.

[List RED ONE's fixes](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tidy%22%2C%22debrief.markFix%22%2C%22track-red-one%22%5D)

media.altText: One of RED ONE's fixes drawn in its own colour with a label beside it.

steps.title: Shear a leg, as in TMA
steps.description:
Shear holds one end of a track and moves the other: every fix moves in proportion to its time from the held end, so a straight leg stays straight with a new course and speed. It is the drag analysts use most on TMA legs. Select BLUE ONE and drag the diamond beside its last fix; the map gives the new course and speed. Letting go is one step.

**Shear track…** is on the track's menu in the Outline.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the diamond and use the arrow keys. Or shear by typing the course and speed made good.

[Shear BLUE ONE](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tidy%22%2C%22debrief.shearTrack%22%2C%22track-blue-one%22%5D)

[Next walkthrough: Annotate and export a figure](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22debrief.debrief%23annotate%22%2Ctrue%5D)

media.altText: BLUE ONE's leg sheared: the start held, the end dragged by its diamond to a new position.

walkthroughs.title: Annotate and export a figure
walkthroughs.description: Draw an annotation, label the times on tracks, export the map as an image that traces to its plot, and find the plot again from the image. About 10 minutes.

steps.title: Open a copy of serial 1
steps.description:
A fresh copy of serial 1, titled Serial 1: Annotate and export a figure. The sample itself never changes.

The copy goes into a catalogue of its own, Walkthrough: Annotate and export a figure.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the button and press Enter.

[Open a copy of serial 1](command:debrief.walkthrough.open?%5B%22annotate%22%5D)

media.altText: The map of serial 1, ready to annotate.

steps.title: Draw an annotation
steps.description:
On the map's toolbar choose **Area**, click each corner and double-click the last: the map gives ranges, bearings and the area as you draw. Name it in the form, such as Search area, and press **Add**. It is one step; drag a corner later to change it.

The toolbar is on the map; **Add annotation…** is on the Outline's title bar.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the map's toolbar and press Enter on **Area**; the arrow keys pan the map under the cross, Space places a corner, Enter finishes. Or add it by typing the positions.

[Add an annotation](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22annotate%22%2C%22debrief.addAnnotation%22%5D)

media.altText: An area drawn on the map in amber, dashed and labelled Search area.

steps.title: Label the times on tracks
steps.description:
Select BLUE ONE and RED ONE, then set their frequencies: labels every 10 min and arrows every 5 min, one step for both. The times sit beside each track on the clock's tens; zoomed out, they thin to round times, and the map says so.

**Frequencies: labels, symbols and arrows…** is on a track's menu in the Outline.

**Keyboard:** Each of labels, symbols and arrows is a list: ↓ to choose, Enter for the next; or type an interval such as 90 s.

[Set BLUE ONE's and RED ONE's frequencies](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22annotate%22%2C%22debrief.setTrackFrequencies%22%2C%5B%22track-blue-one%22%2C%22track-red-one%22%5D%5D)

media.altText: BLUE ONE and RED ONE labelled with their times every 10 minutes, with direction arrows.

steps.title: Export a traceable image
steps.description:
Export the map as a PNG, as a 1600 × 900 slide. It is the map as you see it, labels where the map put them. The image carries an ID naming this plot and the exact step it shows: in its metadata, and in a small footer, such as DBF-PTET-KG8R-B9EM-69, for when Word or PowerPoint drops the metadata. Exporting is never a step.

**Export image…** is the camera on the map's title bar.

**Keyboard:** Each choice is a list or a box to tick: ↓, Space, Enter.

[Export image](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22annotate%22%2C%22debrief.exportImage%22%5D)

media.altText: The exported image: the map with the image's ID in its least busy corner.

steps.title: Find the image's source
steps.description:
Change the plot, then find the image's source: type the ID from its corner (or choose the image file). Debrief opens the plot as it was when the image was exported, read-only, at the view and time exported. **Go to latest** returns to the plot as it is now.

**Find source of image…** is on Catalogues' title bar menu.

**Keyboard:** Type the ID and press Enter; on the map, Tab to **Go to latest** and press Enter.

[Find source of image](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22annotate%22%2C%22debrief.findImageSource%22%5D)

[Next walkthrough: Bearings and TMA](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%5B%22debrief.debrief%23tma%22%2Ctrue%5D)

media.altText: The image's ID leading back to the plot, shown read-only at the step it was exported.

walkthroughs.title: Bearings and TMA
walkthroughs.description: BLUE ONE's towed array on RED ONE, in serial 1, fitted as legacy Debrief's TMA tutorial teaches: keep a side of an ambiguous bearing, make a first guess, put its start at RED ONE's range, shear the first leg to fit, leave out a wild bearing, then split at RED ONE's turn and fit the second leg the same way. About 12 minutes.

steps.title: Open a copy of serial 1 and its bearings
steps.description:
A fresh copy of serial 1, titled Serial 1: Bearings and TMA, with BLUE ONE's towed array selected in the **Outline** and its bearings plotted in **Bearings**, time running up the left, drawn on the map in purple. A towed array cannot tell port from starboard, so each cut has two bearings, mirrored about the array's heading: two lines on the map, the port one solid and the starboard one dashed, and two faint dots in Bearings, until you keep one. One cut has been turned 40° off, as a wild bearing would be; the step that did it is in History. The sample itself never changes.

The copy goes into a catalogue of its own, Walkthrough: Bearings and TMA. **Bearings** opens in the panel below the editor, beside the Terminal, and follows what you select in the **Outline**; drag the panel's top edge up for a taller plot.

**Keyboard:** Tab to the button and press Enter.

[Open a copy of serial 1](command:debrief.walkthrough.open?%5B%22tma%22%5D)

media.altText: BLUE ONE's towed array cuts on the map, each a pair of lines mirrored about the array's heading: one solid to port, one dashed to starboard.

steps.title: Keep a side of an ambiguous bearing
steps.description:
The button opens the towed array in the **Outline**, a row for each of its cuts, and selects the cut at 09:46Z, moving current time there, so the map draws it wider and Bearings rings it. BLUE ONE's Bow sonar is not ambiguous, and at 09:46:00Z it bore 235.3°: open Bow sonar in the Outline to see its cuts. So keep the towed array's bearing that agrees, 236.3° (starboard): **Keep starboard** in **Tools**, or click the cut's line on the map and keep it there. It is one step. The walkthrough keeps this cut's side only: each of the period's other ambiguous cuts, marked ≈ in the Outline, is measured by whichever of its bearings is nearer the solution, and Bearings says so under ⋯. That is an assumption, a fair one once the solution is near; select a run of cuts in the Outline to keep a side for all of them at once.

In the **Outline**, then **Tools** (or the cut's menu in the Outline); or on the map.

**Keyboard:** In the Outline, ↑ and ↓ move along the cuts, → and ← open and close a row, and Enter selects. Then Tab to **Tools** and press Enter on **Keep starboard: this cut**. In the plot, 1 and 2 keep the cut's first or second bearing.

[Choose the cut at 09:46Z](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tma%22%2C%22debrief.chooseInOutline%22%2C%22sensor-blue-one-towed-array%22%2C%7B%22cut_time%22%3A%222023-06-15T09%3A46%3A00.000Z%22%7D%5D)

media.altText: One towed-array cut's two lines, the one kept beside the Bow sonar's line at the same time.

steps.title: Make a first guess
steps.description:
A solution is rooted in a run of a sensor's cuts, chosen in the Outline: open the sensor, click its first cut and Shift-click its last. The button chooses the towed array's 102 cuts from 09:46Z to 12:00Z and runs **TMA solution from 102 cuts 09:46:00Z–12:00:00Z…** in **Tools**, which opens the first guess in Bearings: 10,000 yd (4.94 nmi) along the first cut's bearing, a course across it, 8 kn. Keep Debrief's defaults and press **Make solution**. The solution is drawn on the map, and Bearings plots it with time running up the left: in the **Bearing** pane each cut's measured bearing is a dot and the solution's calculated bearings a line; beside it, the **Error** pane has each cut's bearing less the solution's. An RMS of 56° and ✗ 95 of 102 beyond 3.0° say the guess is far off, as a first guess is. **Two clicks on the map instead** takes the first guess from a click on the first cut's line and one on the last's.

In the **Outline** and **Tools**; the form opens in **Bearings**.

**Keyboard:** In the Outline, Shift with ↓ or ↑ extends the run of cuts. In **Tools**, Enter on **TMA solution from …** opens the form, which has the keyboard; Enter makes the solution.

[Choose the period and open the first guess](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tma%22%2C%22debrief.chooseInOutline%22%2C%22sensor-blue-one-towed-array%22%2C%7B%22period%22%3A%7B%22start%22%3A%222023-06-15T09%3A46%3A00.000Z%22%2C%22end%22%3A%222023-06-15T12%3A00%3A00.000Z%22%7D%2C%22make%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)

media.altText: The first guess, a straight solution heading away across the bearings; in Bearings its errors lie far from zero.

steps.title: Put the start at RED ONE's range
steps.description:
Legacy Debrief's TMA tutorial fits a leg from its start: the start pinned on the first bearing, then the rest fitted to it. The first guess starts on the first bearing, but 4.94 nmi out, and bearings never say how far: an analyst tries a range, fits, and tries another. Here the walkthrough gives it: RED ONE was 3.27 nmi from the towed array at 09:46Z. So move the whole solution 1.67 nmi along the first bearing, towards BLUE ONE: the button opens **Move…** for it; type 1.67 nmi and 056.3. Or drag the square in the middle of the solution on the map, its Move handle, keeping the start on the first cut's line: the lowest dot in the Error pane, at 09:46Z, stays on zero while it is, and the map says how far it has moved. It is one step. The RMS goes up, to 63°: the course and speed are still the guess's. The next step fits them.

**Move track…** is on the solution's menu in the Outline; choose **Whole track**.

**Keyboard:** The form has the keyboard: type the distance, Tab, the bearing, Enter. On the map, Tab to the square and use the arrow keys, Shift for bigger steps; the form keeps the start on the line more easily.

[Move the solution…](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tma%22%2C%22debrief.moveTrack%22%2C%22%24solution%22%5D)

media.altText: The solution moved along the first cut's bearing towards BLUE ONE, its start at RED ONE's range then; the first guess dashed where it was.

steps.title: Shear the first leg to fit
steps.description:
Now hold that start and drag the solution's end, the diamond at its end on the map: a shear. Bearings works the errors out again as you drag, and the Error pane's axis fits them every frame, so a slope in the dots says which way to drag. First drag a box round the errors from 09:46Z to 10:32Z in the Error pane, to zoom in on them; the zoom stays while you drag. Drag until those errors stand straight up the zero line: about 246° at 3.8 kn. Up to 10:32Z all but 2 of the 40 then lie within 3°, an RMS of 1.7° there. After 10:32Z they run away, to −77° by 12:00Z: RED ONE turned, and no straight leg fits both sides of a turn. So the cue still says ✗ 64 of 102 beyond 3.0°, and the RMS is 39°, until the second leg is fitted too. Letting go is one step.

**Shear track…** is on the solution's menu in the Outline; choose **Whole track** and **Hold the start**.

**Keyboard:** In the plot, ↑ and ↓ choose a cut, + zooms time about it and ] the errors; 0 resets. On the map, Tab to the end's diamond and use the arrow keys, Shift for bigger steps. Or type the course and speed made good in the form: 246 and 3.8 kn.

[Shear the solution…](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tma%22%2C%22debrief.shearTrack%22%2C%22%24solution%22%5D)

media.altText: The solution sheared about its start; in Bearings its errors stand on the zero line up to 10:32Z and run away after RED ONE's turn.

steps.title: Leave out a wild bearing
steps.description:
Among the errors running away after the turn, one dot sits some 40° left of its neighbours: the cut at 11:12Z, a wild bearing. The button selects it in the Outline, under the towed array; Bearings keeps the solution shown and rings it. Leave it out of the RMS: **Leave out of Contact 1 solution** in **Tools**, or Space in the plot. It is one step; the cut is still drawn, as a dotted ring. **Count in Contact 1 solution**, or Undo, counts it again. Left out now, it cannot pull the second leg's fit.

In the **Outline**, then **Tools** (or the cut's menu in the Outline).

**Keyboard:** In the Outline, ↑ and ↓ to the cut, Enter, then Tab to **Tools** and Enter on **Leave out of Contact 1 solution**. In the plot, Space or Delete does the same for the cut chosen there.

[Choose the cut at 11:12Z](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tma%22%2C%22debrief.chooseInOutline%22%2C%22%24solution%22%2C%7B%22cut_time%22%3A%222023-06-15T11%3A12%3A00.000Z%22%7D%5D)

media.altText: Bearings' Error pane, the wild bearing at 11:12Z left out, a dotted ring some 40° from its neighbours.

steps.title: Split at the turn and fit the second leg
steps.description:
The button opens the solution in the Outline, a row for its leg and one for each of its positions, and selects its position at 10:38Z, the first after RED ONE's turn, moving current time there. Split before it: **Split before 10:38:00Z** in **Tools** makes it the first position of a new leg, or S in the plot. It is one step, and the solution stays one track, now two legs in the Outline. Then fit the second leg as you fitted the first. On the map choose **This leg**: the handles drag the leg current time is in, now the second, and the first stays where it is. Pin its start: drag its square across the bearing until its lowest error, at 10:38Z, sits on zero, about 0.17 nmi at 155°. Then drag its end until its errors stand up the zero line: about 200° at 5.2 kn. The RMS comes down to 1.8°, as near as these bearings allow: they are good to about 1.5°, so even a perfect fit leaves some beyond 3°. The cue says ✗ 9 of 101 beyond 3.0°, the largest 4.8°, where RED ONE's true track would leave 8: aim for an RMS under about 2° and only a handful beyond. The step is done once a leg is dragged. To go back to the first leg, click it on the map, or select one of its positions in the Outline.

**Split before** is in **Tools** and on the position's menu in the Outline; **Move track…** and **Shear track…** are on the solution's menu; **This leg** is on the map, under What changes.

**Keyboard:** Tab to **Tools** and Enter on **Split before 10:38:00Z**, or S in the plot. On the map, **This leg** is a button; Tab to the square or the end's diamond and use the arrow keys. Or type it: **Move…** and **Shear…** offer the leg under What changes: 0.17 nmi and 155, then 200 and 5.2 kn.

[Choose the position at 10:38Z](command:debrief.walkthrough.do?%5B%22tma%22%2C%22debrief.chooseInOutline%22%2C%22%24solution%22%2C%7B%22fix_time%22%3A%222023-06-15T10%3A38%3A00.000Z%22%7D%5D)

**All walkthroughs done** once this step is done: this is the last walkthrough.

media.altText: The solution in two legs joined at 10:38Z, each fitted; in Bearings the errors stand on the zero line all the way up.

view/title.when: view == debrief.outline && debrief.selectionVisibility != hidden && debrief.selectionVisibility != mixed

debrief.python.markdownDescription: Python interpreter with Debrief's Python packages installed. Leave empty to use `python3`, or `python` on Windows.

debrief.exportFolder.markdownDescription: A folder agents may export images into, besides this workspace's folders. Your own exports go wherever you save them.

debrief.toolTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a tool may run before Debrief stops it.

enumDescriptions: Ask, for each track imported, whether it is plotted over the ground or by dead reckoning.
Plot every track imported over the ground (OTG): each fix where it was logged.
Plot every track imported by dead reckoning (DR): from the first fix, by each fix's course and speed.
debrief.trackImportMode.markdownDescription: How tracks imported from REP files are plotted. Set when you choose *Use this choice for future imports*; set it back to `ask` (or run **Debrief: Ask again whether imported tracks are OTG or DR**) to be asked for each track again. Kept with your Debrief settings, never in a plot.

debrief.tma.errorCutOff.markdownDescription: The Bearings view's error cut-off, in degrees: its Error pane is green while every error counted is within it, and pink otherwise, as legacy Debrief's Stacked Dots shaded it. Also set in the view, beside *Hold scale*. Kept with your Debrief settings, never in a plot.

debrief.map.minimumContextContrast.markdownDescription: Draw tracks outside the time window as Visible (at least 3:1 against the map) even on a plot set to Faint: a plot can never show context fainter than Visible. A plot set to Hidden still hides them.
